title: Treasury coupon announcement (2Y + 5Y + 7Y notes, 13/26/6-week bills) — the leanest and most compressed month-end block in the schedule, sized on Christmas Eve
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 (security, announce, auction, settle) rows spanning 2026-08-05 to 2027-01-28 — the same 213 the 2026-11-19 and 2027-01-21 siblings derived, which is the parse's own cross-check. SIX securities carry announce date `Thursday, December 24, 2026`, read verbatim: `13-Week  BILL`, `26-Week  BILL`, `2-Year  NOTE` and `5-Year  NOTE` (ALL FOUR auctioning Monday, December 28, 2026), plus `6-Week  BILL` and `7-Year  NOTE` (both Tuesday, December 29, 2026). All six settle Thursday, December 31, 2026. Composition INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED and CONFIRMED UNCHANGED against the proposal this file replaces — no correction needed, the second time in this series a proposal has survived a re-read intact. Stays estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the announcement itself. The ~11:00 a.m. ET announcement slot is standing convention inherited from the sibling coupon-announcement ledgers and is NOT separately sourced; see the notes for what was actually tested about the half-day clock. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md — the id previously existed only as `proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-12-24.from-treasury-7y-note-2026-11-25.json` (2026-09-09), which was read in full first and is now shadowed. WHAT MAKES THIS INSTANCE DIFFERENT FROM ITS TWO RESEARCHED SIBLINGS: it is BOTH the leanest and the most compressed month-end block in the whole published schedule. Leanest — six securities and $183B of nominal coupons with NO FRN and NO 52-week bill (against 11-19's eight securities and $211B, and 2027-01-21's seven and $213B); the FRN reopening and the 52-week both fall on the 12-17 announcement instead, the FRN on its quarterly reopening cycle and the 52-week on the strict 28-day cycle the January sibling measured (140 of 152 gaps since 2015 exactly 28 days). Most compressed — the 2-Year and the 5-Year auction on the SAME SESSION (Monday, December 28) and the 7-Year the next day, so three coupon legs clear in TWO sessions rather than the usual three or four. It is the ONLY 2-session block among the six in the schedule's window. THE ONE REAL MEASUREMENT, and it is this series' first non-null: compression costs the compressed legs demand, weakly. Across 125 complete 2Y/5Y/7Y blocks since 2015 (fiscaldata auctions_query, 4,369 rows, re-pulled this session), scored at the BLOCK level (one observation per block — the correct unit, since legs of one block face one market) on the mean z of the 2Y and 5Y legs alone: 25 compressed blocks average z -0.237 against +0.062 for the other 100, diff -0.299, t=-1.42 — NOT significant over the full sample. From 2020-05 onward it is: -0.551 (n=19) vs -0.148 (n=54), diff -0.403, t=-2.67. THE PLACEBO PASSES, which is why the finding is worth registering at all: the 7-Year, the one leg that does NOT share a session, shows nothing in any window (t=-0.17 all years, t=-0.17 from 2020-05) — the drag sits on exactly the legs the mechanism names and is absent from the leg it exempts. THE HONEST OFFSETS: pre-2020 the sign FLIPS (+0.351, n=4, uninformative rather than contradictory); the current size regime has n=7 (t=-1.75, a direction); and 2020-05 was one of five era windows tested, so its p-value is uncorrected. Registered as a forward test, never as a call. A SECOND, SEPARATE METHOD FINDING this calendar should carry forward: the naive version of the same test — pooling the 2Y and 5Y legs as independent observations — reads t=-2.92, roughly twice the clustered statistic. Measured within-block leg correlation is rho=0.239 (375 pairs), a design effect of only 1.24, so clustering explains ~1.11x of that 2.06x and leg-averaging the rest; the lesson holds either way, that a leg-pooled t-statistic in this series overstates its confidence and the block is the unit. DIRECT PRECEDENT, n=2 and named as such: exactly two prior coupon blocks were announced on a December 24 — 2015 (block z -0.546, 25th of 125) and 2020 (block z -0.883, 14th of 125). 2020 is a ROW-FOR-ROW CALENDAR TWIN: announced Thursday 2020-12-24, 2Y and 5Y both auctioning Monday 2020-12-28, 7Y Tuesday 2020-12-29, all settling 2020-12-31 — identical to 2026 because December 2020 and December 2026 share a weekday layout. It printed 2.45 / 2.39 / 2.31 against pool means 2.686 / 2.425 / 2.487. A third weak negative pointing the same way: December blocks as a class run z -0.305 (n=10) vs +0.032 (n=115), t=-1.44. THE CONTENT IS THE EASIEST PART, as in both siblings: 2Y $69B, 5Y $70B, 7Y $44B sit in sb0590's invariant columns (re-read direct this session, HTTP 200, 75,577 bytes — 69/58/70/44 identical in all six published rows May-26 through Oct-26) on a 28-month, nine-refunding freeze in the tape (2Y unchanged since 2024-04-23, 5Y since 2024-04-24, 7Y since 2024-04-25). December-26 is the SECOND cell of the 2026-11-04 refunding's window, so this doc sits exactly between its siblings on guidance distance — weaker than 11-19's first cell, stronger than 2027-01-21's third — and unlike January it HAS a dress rehearsal: the 11-19 announcement reads all three of these legs five weeks early. NO FOMC STRADDLE, which is what separates this from the January sibling: the December meeting is 2026-12-09, nineteen days before the first auction. THE PROPOSAL'S OPEN QUESTION, TESTED AND ANSWERED AS A NEGATIVE RESULT: whether Treasury shifts the ~11:00 ET ANNOUNCEMENT time on a half-day cannot be sourced — treasurydirect.gov's TA_WS securities feed (HTTP 200, 894,225 bytes, read this session) publishes closingTimeCompetitive and closingTimeNoncompetitive and NO announcement-time field at all, and no Treasury dataset carries one. What IS sourced is that Treasury compresses the AUCTION clock on Christmas Eve: every Christmas-Eve bill auction in the record closed at 10:00 AM against the standard 11:30 AM (2018-12-24, 2019-12-24 note at 10:00, 2020-12-24 and 2025-12-24 4-week and 8-week bills). The 4-week and 8-week bills auction ON 2026-12-24 (announced 12-22), so the session runs 10:00 bill close then a ~11:00 announcement into SIFMA's recommended 2:00 p.m. bond close. That is an inference about the announcement, explicitly not a source. TWO OTHERWISE-UNTRACKED AUCTIONS PROPOSED IN THIS PR: treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28 and treasury-5y-note-2026-12-28. treasury-7y-note-2026-12-29 was already proposed by treasury-7y-note-2026-11-25 and is deliberately NOT duplicated. The three bill legs are deliberately not filed: this calendar tracks no bill auction of any tenor, and inventing that class inside an adjacency sweep would be a scope decision, not a discovery. This entry carries symbols: [] and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed; the date is estimate and nothing here licenses an entry.
